value.summary: For each (a,b) in {1,2}^2, represent arbitrary abstract auxiliaries U and V as coordinate tuples by placing U in coordinate a and V in coordinate b and padding the other coordinates with constants. Substitution into the accepted exact tuple-correlation residual gives the residual A_a+B_b-1{a!=b}D-C. The strict-gain implication therefore forces all four residuals to be positive. Adding the two crossed cases and applying the chain rule yields the combined necessary inequality in equation (12).
value.title: Four constant-padding specializations of the tuple residual

value.summary: A dependency-free standard-library checker constructs a strictly positive correlated rational law, passes it through the exact half-skew BSSC product marginals, and evaluates all relevant information quantities in two independent forms. It corroborates each of the four constant-padding residual identities and the crossed-test chain-rule identity; these finite numerical checks do not replace the universal entropy proof.
value.title: Two-letter padding-correlation identity verifier

value.summary: For any finite receiver-skew broadcast channel and arbitrary finite two-letter Marton law P(W,U,V,X_1,X_2), a Marton value strictly above twice the one-letter value requires A_a+B_b>C+1{a!=b}D for every (a,b) in {1,2}^2, with A_a, B_b, C, and D as defined in the claim. Failure of any test rules out a gain, and the crossed tests imply the combined equation (12). For the half-skew BSSC the tests cover arbitrary abstract two-letter auxiliaries without an assumed tuple structure. They are necessary only and establish neither additivity, a gain, nor capacity.
value.title: Four padding-correlation tests for a two-letter Marton gain

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted result directly advances the active objective of pruning possible multiletter Marton gains by strengthening the existing tuple-correlation analysis into four necessary tests for arbitrary two-letter auxiliary laws.
